title: Hurricane Warning issued for Kauai on September 8 as Hurricane Lowell approaches
dek: The National Weather Service Honolulu issued a Hurricane Warning on September 8, 2026 at 2:30 a.m. HST for Hurricane Lowell affecting multiple zones across Kauai. Residents face life-threatening winds of 74 to 110 mph, storm surge of 2 to 4 feet, major flooding rain, and tornado potential.
author: The GoCheckMyNews Desk
key_fact: Residents in affected Kauai areas must shelter in place immediately; evacuations should be complete and all residents must remain in safe locations away from storm surge flooding.
bottom_line: The National Weather Service advisory at https://api.weather.gov/alerts/urn:oid:2.49.0.1.840.0.70f684e7c76e5b16b3da28b009f8cb731099c2bd.005.1.cap carries the full details of affected areas and conditions. Residents must heed all local emergency management instructions and remain in safe shelter away from storm surge and flood-prone areas through at least early Wednesday morning.
body:
The National Weather Service Honolulu issued a Hurricane Warning on Tuesday, September 8, 2026 at 2:30 a.m. HST for Hurricane Lowell affecting multiple locations across Kauai. Residents in the warning zones face imminent life-threatening conditions and must complete all preparations and shelter immediately.
Residents are instructed to now shelter from life-threatening wind and remain in safe locations. The weather service states that last-minute efforts should focus solely on protecting life, as the area is subject to considerable wind damage.
The window of storm surge concern extends through early Wednesday morning. The weather service warns that flood preparations and ordered evacuations must be complete, with evacuees in shelters well away from flood-prone zones. Residents are instructed to remain sheltered and not venture outside.
Major flooding rain is expected. A Flood Watch is in effect with peak rainfall amounts of 2 to 4 additional inches on western Kauai, with locally higher amounts possible.  The weather service warns that extensive impacts from major rainfall flooding may prompt many evacuations and rescues. Rivers and tributaries may rapidly overflow their banks in multiple places. Flood waters can enter many structures within multiple communities, some becoming uninhabitable or washed away, with many locations where flood waters may cover escape routes.
A Tornado Watch is in effect, with conditions favorable for tornadoes. The weather service warns of potential for several tornadoes. Residents should stay within shelter and keep informed of the latest tornado situation.
The threat to life and property spans all hazards: wind, storm surge, flooding rain, and tornado potential. The wind, storm surge, flooding rain, and tornado threat have remained nearly steady from previous assessment, according to the National Weather Service.
